subject: plan-entitlements
seam: src/app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts:173 (stale-paid fence, now :197); src/app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts:52 (ENTITLING_SUB_STATUSES); src/app/api/billing/webhook/route.ts:154 (unknown org throws)
seam_notes: Rule tested: downgrade guard step 3 - compare STATE fetched from the provider, never delivery order or the payload snapshot. A = HEAD: onOrderPaid fences the tier against order.subscription, the snapshot Polar embedded when it BUILT the event; the file's own LIMITATION comment named the stale-active redelivery as the hole. B = currentSubscription(): when a Polar client is configured, polar.subscriptions.get(order.subscriptionId) replaces the snapshot; fetch failure throws so Polar retries; no client -> snapshot. Instrument = route.replay.test.ts, 9 constructed lifecycle sequences replayed through the real handlers over an in-memory plan store and a mutable provider truth, predicate = final org plan != tier owed by the provider's final state. A: 4/9 sequences leave a revoked org on pro (renewal redelivered after revoke; revoke overtaking the renewal; immediate cancel then redelivery; provider unreachable on redelivery). B: 0/9; existing 35 webhook tests unchanged and green; eslint clean. Other two flipped rules: retries-exhausted (Polar `unpaid`) is already outside ENTITLING_SUB_STATUSES and Polar emits subscription.revoked on exhaustion, so the label never sits at past_due forever - the product-side grace bound is owed only if Polar's dunning config changes; unknown org at grant time already throws (:154) = retry, conformant. Cost: one Polar read per renewal order.paid; a webhook-only deployment (no POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN) keeps the snapshot fence and the hole.

subject: session-continuation

a: a broken hook payload (no transcript_path; transcript path that does not exist) exits 0 with empty stderr - a broken trigger reads as a clean turn; an unreadable or empty rule map exits 0 the same way: 0 of 2 broken payloads loud

return_condition: the rule inverts only for a hook whose instrument failure must block the stop (a release-authority or destructive-mutation class); no Stop hook in this tree is in that class, so exit 3 (non-blocking, surfaced to the human) is the right direction here; re-check if a blocking-class hook is ever added
